newsitem.title: USA: Exide gets German approval on battery acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Exide gets German approval on battery acquisitions.

text.p: Exide Corp. received final approval by the German Federal Cartel Office to purchase DETA Akkumulatoranwark GmbH, MAREG Accumulatoren GmbH and Friwi Silberkraft, owned by CEAG AG, the company said Monday.
The approval was the last step to concluding the acquisition. Exide expects the closing to occur in a matter of days.
The CEAG subsidiaries have total sales revenue of DM 300 million. WIth this acquisition, Exide will be the principal automotive battery supplier to BMW, the company said in a release.
Exide also acquires technology in lithium and silver-zinc batteries.

The acquisition "gives Exide the largest most modern traction battery plant in the world with very competitive labor rates as a result of new agreements with the unions," Arthur M. Hawkins, president chief executive officer and chairman of Exide said in the statement.
"The acquisition also gives us the opportunity to do some additional restructuring in Germany mor erapidly than originally planned, which will result in additional savings of at least $10 million."
